authors: Siqi Lai, Zhao Xu, Weijia Zhang, Hao Liu, Hui Xiong
title: LLMLight: Large Language Models as Traffic Signal Control Agents
venue: Proc. ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD 2025); arXiv:2312.16044
contribution: Uses an LLM as the signal-control agent, prompted with real-time traffic state and reasoning step by step, plus LightGPT, a backbone fine-tuned for TSC; on ten real and synthetic datasets it is reported to beat nine traditional/RL baselines and ten general LLMs, with interpretability rated by fifteen human experts.

authors: Maonan Wang, Aoyu Pang, Yuheng Kan, Man-On Pun, Chung Shue Chen, Bo Huang
title: LLM-Assisted Light: Leveraging Large Language Model Capabilities for Human-Mimetic Traffic Signal Control in Complex Urban Environments
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2403.08337
contribution: LA-Light places an LLM at the centre of control and gives it perception and decision tools (static/dynamic traffic queries, existing TSC algorithms); in the authors' simulation platform it adapts without retraining and cuts average waiting time by 20.4% vs. RL controllers under sensor-outage conditions.

authors: Siyao Zhang, Daocheng Fu, Zhao Zhang, Bin Yu, Pinlong Cai
title: TrafficGPT: Viewing, Processing and Interacting with Traffic Foundation Models
venue: Transport Policy, 150, 95-105; arXiv:2309.06719
contribution: Couples ChatGPT with traffic foundation models so the LLM can decompose traffic-management tasks, call tools in sequence and interact with users in natural language; the abstract reports capabilities, not quantitative control results.

authors: Longchao Da, Minquan Gao, Hao Mei, Hua Wei
title: Prompt to Transfer: Sim-to-Real Transfer for Traffic Signal Control with Prompt Learning
venue: Proc. AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI 2024); arXiv:2308.14284
contribution: PromptGAT uses LLM cloze-style prompts to infer how weather, road type and traffic state alter system dynamics, then grounds a DQN agent's actions to those dynamics, narrowing the sim-to-real performance gap.

authors: Longchao Da, Kuanru Liou, Tiejin Chen, Xuesong Zhou, Xiangyong Luo, Yezhou Yang, Hua Wei
title: Open-TI: Open Traffic Intelligence with Augmented Language Model
venue: Springer journal article, DOI 10.1007/s13042-024-02190-8; arXiv:2401.00211
contribution: Tool-augmented LLM that runs traffic analysis end to end (map acquisition, simulation, TSC policy training) through conversation, and demonstrates an agent-to-agent setup where Open-TI passes intent to a control agent (ChatZero) that selects signal actions.

authors: Aoyu Pang, Maonan Wang, Man-On Pun, Chung Shue Chen, Xi Xiong
title: iLLM-TSC: Integration reinforcement learning and large language model for traffic signal control policy improvement
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2407.06025
contribution: LLM-assisted RL: an RL agent proposes the phase and an LLM checks and corrects unreasonable decisions (degraded communication, rare events such as emergency vehicles), reducing average waiting time by 17.5% vs. RL alone under degraded communication.

authors: Zirui Yuan, Siqi Lai, Hao Liu
title: CoLLMLight: Cooperative Large Language Model Agents for Network-Wide Traffic Signal Control
venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2026); arXiv:2503.11739
contribution: Network-level cooperative LLM agents using a spatiotemporal graph of neighbouring intersections, complexity-aware reasoning depth and simulation-feedback fine-tuning of a lightweight LLM; reported to outperform state-of-the-art methods on synthetic and real datasets.

authors: Maonan Wang, Yirong Chen, Aoyu Pang, Yuxin Cai, Chung Shue Chen, Yuheng Kan, Man On Pun
title: VLMLight: Safety-Critical Traffic Signal Control via Vision-Language Meta-Control and Dual-Branch Reasoning Architecture
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025), pp. 39590-39621
contribution: An LLM meta-controller routes routine traffic to a fast RL policy and critical cases to multi-agent LLM reasoning over image-based multi-view intersection input; emergency-vehicle waiting time drops by up to 65% vs. RL-only with <1% degradation in normal conditions.

authors: Qing Guo, Xinhang Li, Junyu Chen, Zheng Guo, Xiaocong Li, Lin Zhang, Lei Li
title: A Dual Large Language Models Architecture with Herald Guided Prompts for Parallel Fine Grained Traffic Signal Control
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2511.00136
contribution: HeraldLight pairs an LLM-Agent that sets fine-grained timings from forecast queues with an LLM-Critic that catches errors and hallucinations; in CityFlow on Jinan, Hangzhou and New York data (224 intersections) it reports a 20.03% reduction in average travel time.

authors: Hua Wei, Chacha Chen, Guanjie Zheng, Kan Wu, Vikash Gayah, Kai Xu, Zhenhui Li
title: PressLight: Learning Max Pressure Control to Coordinate Traffic Signals in Arterial Network
venue: Proc. 25th ACM SIGKDD Int. Conf. on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining (KDD 2019), pp. 1290-1298
contribution: Grounds the RL reward in max-pressure theory (linked to throughput maximisation) with a compact state, outperforming conventional and prior learning-based controllers on arterials.

authors: Hua Wei, Nan Xu, Huichu Zhang, Guanjie Zheng, Xinshi Zang, Chacha Chen, Weinan Zhang, Yanmin Zhu, Kai Xu, Zhenhui Li
title: CoLight: Learning Network-level Cooperation for Traffic Signal Control
venue: Proc. 28th ACM Int. Conf. on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM 2019); arXiv:1905.05717
contribution: Uses graph attention so neighbouring signal agents communicate and coordinate, reported to outperform state-of-the-art methods on a network with hundreds of signals.

authors: Chacha Chen, Hua Wei, Nan Xu, Guanjie Zheng, Ming Yang, Yuanhao Xiong, Kai Xu, Zhenhui Li
title: Toward A Thousand Lights: Decentralized Deep Reinforcement Learning for Large-Scale Traffic Signal Control
venue: Proc. AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 34(04), 3414-3421
contribution: MPLight: decentralized deep RL using pressure-based regional coordination and a reward that lets agents coordinate implicitly, demonstrated on a real-world Manhattan network of 2,510 traffic lights.

authors: Guanjie Zheng, Yuanhao Xiong, Xinshi Zang, Jie Feng, Hua Wei, Huichu Zhang, Yong Li, Kai Xu, Zhenhui Li
title: Learning Phase Competition for Traffic Signal Control
venue: Proc. 28th ACM Int. Conf. on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM 2019), pp. 1963-1972
contribution: FRAP models competition between phases by demand, giving invariance to flips/rotations, faster convergence and better generalisation across intersection structures.

authors: Afshin Oroojlooy, Mohammadreza Nazari, Davood Hajinezhad, Jorge Silva
title: AttendLight: Universal Attention-Based Reinforcement Learning Model for Traffic Signal Control
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33 (NeurIPS 2020)
contribution: A single attention-based policy that handles intersections with different numbers of roads, lanes and phases without retraining, outperforming classical and RL baselines in single- and multi-environment regimes.

authors: Liang Zhang, Qiang Wu, Jun Shen, Linyuan Lü, Bo Du, Jianqing Wu
title: Expression might be enough: representing pressure and demand for reinforcement learning based traffic signal control
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2112.10107 (v3, 2022)
contribution: Proposes Advanced-MP (counting running and queued vehicles) and the ATS state representation, yielding Advanced-MPLight and Advanced-CoLight that reach state-of-the-art results on real-world datasets.

authors: Qiang Wu, Liang Zhang, Jun Shen, Linyuan Lü, Bo Du, Jianqing Wu
title: Efficient Pressure: Improving efficiency for signalized intersections
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2112.02336
contribution: Introduces efficient pressure (EP) and builds Efficient-MP and the Efficient-XLight RL family, evaluated on multiple real-world datasets.

authors: Huichu Zhang, Siyuan Feng, Chang Liu, Yaoyao Ding, Yichen Zhu, Zihan Zhou, Weinan Zhang, Yong Yu, Haiming Jin, Zhenhui Li
title: CityFlow: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Environment for Large Scale City Traffic Scenario
venue: The World Wide Web Conference (WWW 2019); arXiv:1905.05217
contribution: A fast, scalable microscopic simulator for city-scale multi-agent RL, the default platform for most PressLight/CoLight/LLMLight-family studies.

authors: Pablo Alvarez Lopez, Michael Behrisch, Laura Bieker-Walz, Jakob Erdmann, Yun-Pang Flötteröd, Robert Hilbrich, Leonhard Lücken, Johannes Rummel, Peter Wagner, Evamarie Wießner
title: Microscopic Traffic Simulation using SUMO
venue: 21st IEEE Int. Conf. on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSC 2018), pp. 2575-2582
contribution: Reference description of the open-source SUMO microscopic simulator widely used for TSC, V2X and CAV studies.

authors: Lucas N. Alegre
title: SUMO-RL
venue: GitHub repository (software)
contribution: Gymnasium/PettingZoo-compatible RL environments for traffic signal control on top of SUMO.

authors: James Ault, Guni Sharon
title: Reinforcement Learning Benchmarks for Traffic Signal Control
venue: Proc. NeurIPS Track on Datasets and Benchmarks, Vol. 1 (2021)
contribution: RESCO toolkit and realistic SUMO benchmark scenarios; finds earlier methods are brittle to changed sensing assumptions and irregular intersections.

authors: Hao Mei, Xiaoliang Lei, Longchao Da, Bin Shi, Hua Wei
title: LibSignal: An Open Library for Traffic Signal Control
venue: Machine Learning (Springer), DOI 10.1007/s10994-023-06412-y; arXiv:2211.10649
contribution: Open library benchmarking RL-TSC models across both SUMO and CityFlow with calibrated environments and shared protocols.

authors: Arthur Müller, Vishal Rangras, Georg Schnittker, Michael Waldmann, Maxim Friesen, Tobias Ferfers, Lukas Schreckenberg, Florian Hufen, Jürgen Jasperneite, Marco Wiering
title: Towards Real-World Deployment of Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control
venue: 20th IEEE Int. Conf. on Machine Learning and Applications (ICMLA 2021), DOI 10.1109/ICMLA52953.2021.00085; arXiv:2103.16223
contribution: LemgoRL: a realistic benchmark of the German town of Lemgo with a signal-logic unit enforcing regulatory and safety constraints, aimed at deployable RL.

authors: Pravin Varaiya
title: Max pressure control of a network of signalized intersections
venue: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies (2013)
contribution: Introduces max-pressure control for signalized networks: a decentralized policy using only local queue information with a proven maximum-throughput (queue-stability) property.

authors: Michael W. Levin
title: Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Timing: A Summary of Methodological and Experimental Results
venue: Journal of Transportation Engineering, Part A: Systems, 149(4)
contribution: State-of-the-art review of max-pressure variants (cycle-based, realistic flow models, measurement error, multimodal access) and their simulation and early field evidence.

authors: Raphael Stern, Michael W. Levin, Amir Kiani
title: Toward Implementation of Max-Pressure Control on Minnesota Roads: Phase 2
venue: Minnesota Department of Transportation, Report MN 2024-26
contribution: Hardware-in-the-loop testbed running max-pressure on a Q-Free MaxTime controller, showing MP can be safely deployed on North American signal hardware.

authors: Qiangqiang Guo, Li Li, Xuegang (Jeff) Ban
title: Urban traffic signal control with connected and automated vehicles: A survey
venue: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies, 101, 313-334
contribution: Surveys CAV-enabled state estimation and signal optimisation, groups CAV-based control into six types under a common framework and outlines research directions.

authors: Yiheng Feng, K. Larry Head, Shayan Khoshmagham, Mehdi Zamanipour
title: A real-time adaptive signal control in a connected vehicle environment
venue: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies, 55, 460-473
contribution: Two-level phase-sequence/duration optimisation from connected-vehicle data with estimation of unequipped vehicles; in VISSIM it cuts total delay up to 16.33% vs. actuated control at high penetration but is similar at low penetration.

authors: Vindula Jayawardana, Cathy Wu
title: Learning Eco-Driving Strategies at Signalized Intersections
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2204.12561
contribution: RL eco-driving for CAVs at signals: up to 18% fuel and 25% CO2 reduction at full penetration, with 25% penetration delivering at least half of the benefit.

authors: Marie-Ange Lebre, Frédéric Le Mouël, Eric Ménard, Alexandre Garnault, Benazouz Bradaï, Vanessa Picron
title: Real scenario and simulations on GLOSA traffic light system for reduced CO2 emissions, waiting time and travel time
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:1506.01965
contribution: Evaluates Green Light Optimal Speed Advisory with real driving and simulation across V2I penetration rates, reporting reduced CO2, waiting and travel time.

authors: Zhongxia Yan, Cathy Wu
title: Reinforcement Learning for Mixed Autonomy Intersections
venue: IEEE Int. Intelligent Transportation Systems Conference (ITSC 2021), DOI 10.1109/ITSC48978.2021.9565000; arXiv:2111.04686
contribution: Multi-agent RL controlling a fraction of vehicles at unsignalized intersections; learned policies behave like signals and reach near-optimal throughput with 33-50% controlled vehicles.

authors: Kaiwen Zhang, Zhiyong Cui, Wanjing Ma
title: A survey on reinforcement learning-based control for signalized intersections with connected automated vehicles
venue: Transport Reviews, 44(6), 1187-1208
contribution: Systematic review of RL for CV/CAV-data signal control, RL trajectory planning for CAVs and cooperative signal-CAV control, with a research roadmap.

authors: Longchao Da, Hao Mei, Romir Sharma, Hua Wei
title: Uncertainty-aware Grounded Action Transformation towards Sim-to-Real Transfer for Traffic Signal Control
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2307.12388
contribution: UGAT applies grounded action transformation only when its uncertainty is low, narrowing the transition-dynamics gap between simulator and target environment for RL-TSC.

authors: Hao Mei, Junxian Li, Bin Shi, Hua Wei
title: Reinforcement Learning Approaches for Traffic Signal Control under Missing Data
venue: Proc. 32nd Int. Joint Conf. on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI 2023), DOI 10.24963/ijcai.2023/251
contribution: Imputes missing states (and rewards) so RL controllers keep working at intersections without sensors, staying robust across missing-data rates.

authors: Wenlu Du, Junyi Ye, Jingyi Gu, Jing Li, Hua Wei, Guiling Wang
title: SafeLight: A Reinforcement Learning Method toward Collision-free Traffic Signal Control
venue: Proc. AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 37(12), 14801-14810
contribution: Safety-enhanced residual RL with multi-objective loss and reward shaping based on road-safety standards, significantly reducing collisions while improving mobility.

authors: James Ault, Josiah P. Hanna, Guni Sharon
title: Learning an Interpretable Traffic Signal Control Policy
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:1912.11023
contribution: Learns regulatable polynomial (interpretable) signal policies via modified Deep Q-learning, reducing delay up to 19.4% vs. actuated control while remaining inspectable.

authors: Dickens Kwesiga, Angshuman Guin, Khaled Abdelghany, Michael Hunter
title: Evaluating the Robustness of Reinforcement Learning based Adaptive Traffic Signal Control
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.15283
contribution: RL controller with field-realistic eight-phase ring-barrier structure cuts delay 11-32% vs. optimised actuated control but degrades under substantially different O-D demand unless trained on diverse patterns.

authors: Ferdous Al Rafi, Susrik Mukherjee, Latika Liladhar Dekate, Jennifer Yawa Lavoe, Huaiyuan Yao, Shlok Mohanty, Longchao Da, Xuesong Zhou, Hua Wei
title: Sim2Signal: Sim-to-Real Benchmarks for Traffic Signal Control
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.01676
contribution: Decomposes the sim-to-real gap into observation, action, transition and reward gaps and tests 18 mitigation methods over 33 gap settings and 10 calibrated networks; direct transfer always degrades and no mitigation wins everywhere.

authors: Xiaocai Zhang, Neema Nassir, Lok Sang Chan, Milad Haghani
title: Human-Centric Traffic Signal Control for Equity: A Multi-Agent Action Branching Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.02959
contribution: MA2B-DDQN rewards minimising the number of delayed people (pedestrians, occupants, transit riders) on a Melbourne corridor, shifting TSC objectives from vehicles to travellers.

authors: Tong Nie, Jian Sun, Wei Ma
title: Exploring the Roles of Large Language Models in Reshaping Transportation Systems: A Survey, Framework, and Roadmap
venue: Elsevier journal article, DOI 10.1016/j.ait.2025.100003; arXiv:2503.21411
contribution: LLM4TR framework classifying LLM roles in transportation as information processors, knowledge encoders, component generators and decision facilitators, with a research roadmap.

authors: Muhammad Monjurul Karim, Yan Shi, Shucheng Zhang, Bingzhang Wang, Mehrdad Nasri, Yinhai Wang
title: Large Language Models and Their Applications in Roadway Safety and Mobility Enhancement: A Comprehensive Review
venue: Elsevier journal article, DOI 10.1016/j.ait.2025.100004; arXiv:2506.06301
contribution: Reviews LLM adaptation for mobility (including signal control) and safety, V2X/edge enablers, and names hallucination, reasoning deficits, data governance and safety assurance as key challenges.
